comments.body:
## ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED BY EXPERIMENT — bug is LIVE. Filed mechanism is WRONG; the real one is broader.

Phase 1 (Understand) only, per scope limit. No tracked file touched. Worktree
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam` @ `144bb02251`. Probes: `/tmp/parity-probe/probe.py`,
`/tmp/parity-probe/probe2.py`.

### AC-1 SETTLED: an errored result carries `decision = "dropped"`

Not inferred from the type — observed from the ONE production constructor of an errored
`ItemRecord` in the repo:

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:174`

    return ItemRecord(valid=False, decision="dropped", errored=True, label=label)

Reached at `fidelity_spot_eval.py:168-174`: every epoch that raises is recorded as the sentinel
`"__error__"` (:171); if NO epoch survives (`if not live:` :173) the item becomes the errored
record above. `label` is the gold label and is PRESERVED across the error.

E1 observed: `decision='dropped'`, `in _DECISIONS: True`, `label='block'` preserved.

This is the only `errored=True` construction under `src/` (the other three hits are in
`tests/unit/test_parity_bar.py:114,231` and the `_rec` helper at :20-21 — and they use the same
`decision="dropped"` shape, so the test corpus encodes this convention too).

### The filed mechanism is REJECTED — and the truth is worse

The ticket says the pair "stays in `gold_pairs`" *because* `dropped` is a member of `_DECISIONS`.
That is not the mechanism. `src/rebar/llm/parity.py:105`:

    gold_pairs = [(a, b) for a, b in pairs if a.label in _DECISIONS]

The filter tests `a.**label**` — the gold label from the corpus item — NOT `a.decision`.
`_DECISIONS` is doing double duty here: as the decision vocabulary AND as the gold-label
vocabulary.

E3 is the discriminating experiment. I gave the errored side a decision OUTSIDE `_DECISIONS`
(`decision="__error__"`), which under the filed mechanism should have excluded the pair:

    E3 decision OUTSIDE _DECISIONS: flips= 1  n_gold= 20  passed= False

The pair was retained and the flip was still counted. So the "latent hazard" escape hatch the
ticket reserved DOES NOT EXIST: **no** value of `decision` on an errored record can exempt the
pair from `gold_pairs`, because `decision` is never consulted for membership. Changing
`fidelity_spot_eval.py:174` to emit some out-of-vocabulary decision would NOT fix this.

The actual root cause, stated precisely:

> `src/rebar/llm/parity.py:107`
>     `decision_flips = sum(1 for a, b in gold_pairs if a.decision != b.decision)`
> compares the `decision` field of both sides of every gold-labelled pair with no `errored`
> guard, while `parity.py:105` admits a pair to `gold_pairs` on its gold `label` alone. An
> errored side carries a SYNTHETIC decision (`"dropped"`, `fidelity_spot_eval.py:174`) that was
> never produced by the model; the comparison at :107 cannot tell a synthetic decision from a
> model verdict, so any errored side whose synthetic decision differs from the other side's real
> verdict is scored as a decision flip. `err1, err2` are computed at `parity.py:102` and are
> available at :107 but are not used there.

(Note the line is :107 on current `origin/main`, not :106 as filed — :106 is `n_gold = len(gold_pairs)`.)

### AC-2 territory: one transient throttle fails the bar

E2 — 20 gold pairs, both arms unanimous `block`, then ONE v2 record replaced with the production
errored record:

    baseline:            flips=0  passed=True
    one transient error: flips=1  n_gold=20  passed=False
      - validity regressed: v2 0.950 < v1 1.000
      - validity 0.950 below floor 0.99
      - 1 decision-level flip(s) on the gold set (must be 0)
      - recall dropped 0.050 > margin 0.02
      - error rate regressed: v2 0.050 > v1 0.000

E5 reproduced this end-to-end through the LIVE driver `parity.parallel_run_and_diff`
(`parity.py:286-302`) with a runner that raises `ThrottlingException` exactly once on the v2 arm:
identical result, `flips=1`, `passed=False`. So the defect fires through the real entry point, not
only via hand-built records.

Confirms the ticket's stated impact for S6 (0d76): a single Bedrock throttle fails criterion (b)
— "ZERO decision-level flips ... never acceptable (it changes what ships)" — and the epic would
read a transient infrastructure event as a Bedrock model-quality regression.

### AC-3 territory: the report CANNOT distinguish a fabricated flip from a real one

E4/probe2 — three v2 arms against the same clean v1, all producing `decision_flips=3`:

    A  3 real flips, 0 errors   decision_flips=3  err_rate_v2=0.00  valid_v2=1.00
    B  2 real flips + 1 error   decision_flips=3  err_rate_v2=0.05  valid_v2=0.95
    C  0 real flips, 3 errors   decision_flips=3  err_rate_v2=0.15  valid_v2=0.85

The gating-failure string is byte-identical in all three: `3 decision-level flip(s) on the gold
set (must be 0)`. `ParityReport.metrics` keys are exactly
`{cost, decision_flips, error_rate, false_accept, latency_s, n, n_gold, recall, validity,
verdict_agreement}` — there is NO per-pair detail, no invalid/excluded count, no index. So:

- `error_rate` tells a reader that SOME error occurred somewhere in the arm, but not WHICH pairs,
  and therefore not how many of the reported flips are fabricated. Case C (zero genuine flips) is
  not distinguishable from case A (three genuine flips) by any single metric — only by inference
  from a coincidence of counts, which breaks as soon as an error lands on a pair the two arms
  already agreed on.
- The corroborating `validity`/`error_rate` movement exists ONLY because
  `fidelity_spot_eval.py:174` happens to couple `errored=True` with `valid=False`. Nothing in
  `ItemRecord` (`parity.py:40-56`) enforces that coupling. Probe2 confirms an
  `errored=True, valid=True` record yields `flips=1, validity_v2=1.0` — a completely silent
  fabricated flip with no corroborating signal at all.

So AC-3 is currently UNMET and a reader necessarily can mistake one for the other.

### Defect legitimacy: `defect`, with a cited in-repo contract

Not the reporter's expectation — the module's own documented contract:

- `parity.py:46` — `errored: bool = False  # a runtime error / timeout (not a model verdict)`.
  The field is documented as explicitly NOT a model verdict.
- `parity.py:10-11` — criterion (b) is `per-criterion verdict AGREEMENT >= 95% AND ZERO
  decision-level flips`. A verdict metric.
- `parity.py:13` — criterion (d) is `runtime ERROR/timeout rate v2 <= v1`. Errors ALREADY have
  their own, separate gating criterion.

Scoring an errored side's synthetic decision under (b) both violates the :46 contract (a
non-verdict is counted as a verdict) and double-counts the same event under (b) and (d) — visible
in E2, where one throttle trips four independent gating failures.

### Hypotheses rejected, with evidence

1. REJECTED — "the pair stays in `gold_pairs` because `dropped ∈ _DECISIONS`" (the filed
   mechanism). E3: an out-of-vocabulary decision is retained and still counted. Membership is
   decided by `label` at `parity.py:105`, never by `decision`.
2. REJECTED — "this may be a latent hazard, not a live bug; reclassify if the decision resolves
   outside `_DECISIONS`". Both branches of that conditional now fail: the production decision IS
   `dropped` (E1, in-vocabulary), AND out-of-vocabulary would not have saved it either (E3).
   **No reclassification is warranted — the bug is LIVE as a `bug`.**
3. REJECTED — "`error_rate` already lets a reader discount fabricated flips". Probe2 B/C: the
   arm-level rate does not localize to pairs, and an `errored=True, valid=True` record moves
   `error_rate` while leaving validity untouched and the flip silent.
4. NOT the cause — `fidelity_spot_eval.py:174` choosing `"dropped"`. It is the proximate source of
   the synthetic decision and is worth revisiting, but E3 proves the defect survives any choice
   made there. The changeable artifact is the missing `errored` guard at `parity.py:107`.

### Scope note

Stopping at the proven root cause per instruction. NOT entering Phase 2 — story 0d76 (S6) is
`in_progress` and owns the parity surface. No fix written, no tracked file modified.

## Fix implemented; offline re-score confirms it changes NOTHING on the recorded run

Commit `5136f91cef` on `feat/0d76-bedrock-parity`. Not pushed to Gerrit; ticket left open.

### What changed

`parity.py` now excludes a gold pair from `decision_flips` when EITHER side has
`errored=True`, counts those into a new `errored_pairs` metric, and names the exclusion in the
flip gating string. The guard reads `errored`, not decision-vocabulary membership, exactly as
the filed root cause requires. The module docstring's criterion (b) was updated to match.

### Re-score of the recorded live run — zero model calls

Predicted no change; measured no change. Both slots re-score byte-identically to the post-Fix-1
values, with `errored_pairs=0`:

| slot | flips | errored_pairs | agreement | validity | error rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| standard | 1 | 0 | 0.964 | 1.000/1.000 | 0.000 |
| frontier | 2 | 0 | 0.929 | 1.000/1.000 | 0.000 |

Two independent reasons this data cannot exercise the guard, both verified:

1. `provider_parity._drop_errored_pairs` already removes errored pairs upstream of
   `parity_report` — a harness-level workaround added for THIS bug, whose docstring cites this
   ticket id. So the scored set is 28 of 30 items and carries no errored record at all.
2. Even scoring the raw 30 records with the drop bypassed, the flip counts are unchanged (2 and
   1). The recorded run's 2 errored items per slot errored on BOTH arms with the same synthetic
   `dropped` decision, so they never produced a fabricated flip. They were the two
   `plan-review-container` G3 fixtures that raise before any model call for want of a `children`
   payload, per the artifact's own `corpus_note`.

So this fix neither helps nor hurts the Bedrock verdict. It removes the latent failure mode.

### Follow-up worth considering (NOT done here)

`_drop_errored_pairs` is now redundant with the guard for the flip criterion, but it is NOT a
pure duplicate: it also keeps errored items out of the validity and error-rate denominators,
which the guard does not. Removing it would change `validity` from 1.000 to 0.933 and the error
rate from 0.000 to 0.067 on both recorded slots (measured). That is a separate decision about
which denominator is correct and was deliberately left alone.

compiled_state.description:
# parity `decision_flips` counts an errored pair as a decision flip

## Context / Problem

An errored side of a paired parity run is scored as a DECISION FLIP. Criterion (b) treats a flip as
never acceptable ("it changes what ships"), so a single transient throttle fails a parity slot as a
model-quality regression.

Proven by experiment through the real entry point (recorded in this ticket's existing comment):
20 gold pairs, both arms unanimous `block`, one v2 record replaced by the production errored record
-> `flips=1, n_gold=20, passed=False`. Re-run end to end through the live driver
`parallel_run_and_diff` (`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:286-302`) with a runner raising
`ThrottlingException` exactly once: identical. One throttle trips four gating failures, including the
never-acceptable criterion.

### The mechanism

`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:107`

    decision_flips = sum(1 for a, b in gold_pairs if a.decision != b.decision)

compares `decision` on both sides of every gold-labelled pair with NO `errored` guard, while an
errored side carries a SYNTHETIC decision no model produced. `err1, err2` are computed at
`parity.py:102` and are unused.

The sole production constructor of an errored record is
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:174`:

    return ItemRecord(valid=False, decision="dropped", errored=True, label=label)

`parity.py:46` documents the contract this violates: `errored` is "a runtime error / timeout (not a
model verdict)". Criterion (d) at `parity.py:128` already gates runtime error rate separately, so
scoring an error under (b) both contradicts `:46` and double-counts one event.

### Two things that look like the mechanism and are NOT

1. It is NOT that the pair survives because `dropped` is a member of `_DECISIONS`. The filter at
   `parity.py:105` is `if a.label in _DECISIONS` — it tests the GOLD LABEL, never `decision`.
   A discriminating experiment gave the errored side `decision="__error__"`, outside `_DECISIONS`,
   and the pair was still retained and counted. NO value of `decision` can exempt an errored pair.
2. It is therefore NOT fixable by changing what `fidelity_spot_eval.py:174` emits; the defect survives
   any value it could pick. That file is out of scope.

The changeable artifact is the missing `errored` guard at `parity.py:107`.

### The silent case

The corroborating validity/error movement that might let a careful reader notice something is off
exists ONLY because `fidelity_spot_eval.py:174` happens to couple `errored=True` with `valid=False`.
Nothing in `ItemRecord` (`parity.py:40-56`) enforces that pairing. A record with
`errored=True, valid=True` yields `flips=1, validity_v2=1.0` — a completely silent fabricated flip.

### The report cannot distinguish fabricated flips from real ones

Three v2 arms against the same v1, all reporting `decision_flips=3` — (A) 3 real / 0 errors,
(B) 2 real + 1 error, (C) 0 real / 3 errors — produce a BYTE-IDENTICAL gating string. `metrics` has
no per-pair detail and no excluded count.

## Approach

Add an `errored` guard to the flip computation at `parity.py:107`: a gold pair where EITHER side has
`errored=True` is excluded from `decision_flips` and counted instead into a new metric
`errored_pairs`, which is surfaced in `ParityReport.metrics` and appended to the flip gating-failure
string so arms (A), (B) and (C) are no longer byte-identical.

The guard reads `a.errored or b.errored` — the field the `parity.py:46` contract already defines as
"not a model verdict" — rather than any decision-vocabulary membership test, because the
discriminating experiment above proved decision-vocabulary tests are a no-op here. Excluding rather
than re-scoring is correct because criterion (d) at `parity.py:128` already gates the error rate: the
event is not lost, it is attributed once to the criterion that owns it instead of twice.

## Scope

* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — guard the `decision_flips` comprehension at `:107`, compute
  `errored_pairs`, add it to the `metrics` dict at `:139-153`, and include it in the flip failure
  string at `:121`. Update the module docstring's criterion (b) wording at `:10-11`.
* `tests/unit/test_parity_bar.py` — add the errored-pair exclusion tests.
* `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` — existing `decision_flips` assertions re-checked; updated only
  where the errored guard legitimately changes an expected value.

## Testing

* An errored pair (production shape `valid=False, decision="dropped", errored=True`) opposite a real
  `block` verdict is excluded from `decision_flips` and reported as errored; RED before the change.
* The silent variant `errored=True, valid=True` is covered specifically, since no other signal
  catches it.
* A genuine flip between two non-errored sides is STILL counted — the guard must not suppress real
  regressions.
* Arms (A) 3 real / 0 errors, (B) 2 real + 1 error and (C) 0 real / 3 errors produce three DIFFERENT
  report outputs, asserted by comparing their gating-failure strings and `errored_pairs` values
  pairwise.
* Each new test is mutation-checked in both directions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An errored pair is excluded from `decision_flips` and reported separately, with the guard at
      `parity.py:107` reading `errored` rather than any decision-vocabulary membership test; verified
      by a unit test asserting `decision_flips == 0` and a non-zero errored count on a one-errored-pair
      run that previously reported `decision_flips == 1`.
- [ ] A test constructs a paired run where exactly one side errored and asserts it is not counted as a
      flip; it fails before the fix, verified by running it against the unmodified source.
- [ ] A test covers the `errored=True, valid=True` record specifically; it fails before the fix.
- [ ] A test asserts a genuine flip between two non-errored sides is still counted, so the guard does
      not mask real regressions.
- [ ] Arms (A), (B) and (C) above produce non-identical report output; verified by a test asserting
      pairwise inequality of their gating-failure strings.
- [ ] Re-scoring the recorded run at `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json` with this
      guard changes no metric, since that run has a 0.000 error rate on all four arms; verified by an
      offline re-score with zero model calls and recorded as a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code, and the default test selection is green.

file_impact.reason: guard decision_flips on errored and report errored pairs separately
add errored-pair exclusion and distinguishability tests
